definitions.full: H5248. Nimrod נִמְרוֺד נִמְרֹד, proper name, masculine Nimrod (etymology and meaning wholly unknown; Thes (dubious) below מָרַד rebel (of which Hebr. may have thought [compare Lag BN 105 ]); in fact probably Babylonian name; 1 = a god e.g. Marduk, We compare Hexateuch (2), 308 f.; Nimrod, Encycl. Brit. (9). xvii. 511 , RS Semitic i. 91 n .; 2d ed. 92; Hom PSBA xv (1893), 291-300 proposes Narûdu = *Namra-uddu , a star-god. 2 < name of Babylonian king or prince: Nu-marad = 'Man of Marad' compare Dl Pa 220 De Gen 10:8 [1887]; more plausibly = Nazi-maraddash ( marattash, murudas ), Hpt AR July, 1884, 93 f. Dl K (1884) Say Ath. Feb. 16, 1895, Acad. Mar. 2, 1895 (compare Che ib. Mar. 9 ), — i.e. a Kashite king, B.C. 1378, but dubious, compare Hpt BAS i (1889), 183 , Jerem Izdubar-Nimrod, 1891, 1 ff. ); — son of כּוּשׁ (q. v.), hero and hunter 10:8-9 , (J; king in Babylonia, builder of Nineveh, etc. 10:10 f.), נִמְרוֺד 1Chr 1:10 ; נִמְרֹד אֶרֶץ Micah 5:5 (|| אַשּׁוּר אֶרֶץ ); ᵐ5 Νεβρωδ .
